of a place. —हरि-शयन, अम्, n. the sleep of Viṣṇu. —हरि-शर, अस्, m. ‘having Viṣṇu for an arrow,’ epithet of Śiva, (Viṣṇu having served Śiva as the shaft which set the cities of Tripura on fire.) —हरि-शर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a poet. —हरि-शिप्र, अस्, m., Ved. ‘ruddy-jawed,’ epithet of Indra. —हरि-श्चन्द्र, अस्, आ, अम् (see चन्द्र), Ved. having golden-coloured splendor; after enduring incredible sufferings, Hari-ścandra won the pity of the gods and was raised with his subjects to heaven; on the other hand, in the Sabhā-parvan of the Mahā-bhārata, verse 489 &c., his performance of the Rāja-sūya sacrifice is stated to have been the cause of his elevation, and in the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa quite another legend is told about him, see under शुनः-शेप, p. 1014: in later legends Hari-ścandra is represented as insidiously induced by Nārada to relate his actions with unbecoming pride, whereupon he was degraded from Svarga, one stage at each sentence, till stopping in time and doing homage to the gods he was fixed with his capital in mid-air; हरिक: हरिक, अस्, m. a horse of a yellowish or reddish brown colour (= हालक); a thief, (in this sense evidently fr. rt. 1. हृ); a gambler with dice.
हरिण: हरिण, अस्, ई, अम् (the fem. may equally belong to हरित, next col.), greenish or yellowish or reddish white, pale, whitish; (अस्), m. yellowish or reddish white (the colour); white (the colour); a deer, ante-lope, fawn, stag (one of five kinds, others being called ऋष्य, रुरु, पृषत, मृग); a goose; a minor division of the world; the sun; N. of Viṣṇu; of Śiva; (ई), f. green (the colour); yellow jasmine; a female deer, doe; a golden image; one of the four kinds of women, an excellent woman (= चि-त्रिणी, corresponding to the kind of man termed मृग); turmeric (= हरिता); madder (= मञ्-जिष्ठा); a species of the Aty-aṣṭi metre (= त-रुणी). —हरिण-कलङ्क, अस्, m. ‘deer-spotted,’ epithet of the moon. —हरिण-धामन्, आ, m. the moon. —हरिण-नयन, अस्, ई, अम्, deer-eyed, fawn-eyed, having eyes like a deer. —हरिण-नर्तक, अस्, m. a minstrel of Indra's heaven (= किन्-नर). —हरिण-प्लुत, अम्, आ, n. f. a kind of metre (described by some as a stanza having eleven syllables in every first and third Pāda, and twelve in every second and fourth; by others two kinds of metre are given). —हरिण-लोचन = हरिण-न-यन. —हरिण-हृदय, अस्, आ, अम्, deer-hearted, faint-hearted, timid. —हरिणाक्ष (°ण-अक्°), अस्, ई, अम्, deer-eyed, fawn-eyed; (अस्), m. epithet of Śiva; (ई), f. a woman with beautiful eyes; a kind of perfume (= हट्ट-विलासिनी). —हरिणाङ्क (°ण-अङ्°), अस्, m. ‘deer-marked,’ the moon; [cf. ह-रिण-कलङ्क।] —हरिणान्तर (°ण-अन्°), अस्, m. a species of deer (= भार्याटिक).
हरिणाय: हरिणाय, Nom. A. हरिणायते, &c., to become a deer.
हरिणी: हरिणी, see under हरिण. —हरिणी-वृत्त, अम्, n. the Hariṇī metre.
हरित्: हरित्, त्, त्, त् (in Uṇādi-s. हरित: हरित, अस्, आ or हरिणी, अम् (connected with हरिण above; cf. its fem. हरिणी; cf. also 2. भ-रित with its fem. भरिणी), green, of a green colour; reddish brown or tawny; grassy, verdant; dark blue; (अस्), m. green (the colour); a lion; a kind of grass (= मन्थानक); N. of a son of Yuvanāśva; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a Gotra; (आ), f. हरितक: हरितक, अस्, m. a green vegetable, pot-herb.
हरिताय: हरिताय, Nom. A. हरितायते, &c., to become green or verdant.
हरितायत्: हरितायत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, becoming green.
हरिताल: हरिताल, अस्, m. a kind of pigeon of a yellowish green colour; (ई), f. हरितालक: हरितालक, अस्, m. a kind of pigeon of a yellowish green colour; (अम्), n. yellow orpiment; painting the person, theatrical decoration.
हरितालिका: हरितालिका, f. Dūrvā grass; the fourth day of the light half of the month Bhādra. —हरितालिका-व्रत, अम्, n. a particular religious observance on the above day.

2. हरिमन्, आ, m. (for. 1. see p. 1167), time.
हरिय: हरिय, अस्, m. a horse of a yellowish or reddish colour.
हरीतकी: हरीतकी, f. the yellow Myrobalan tree, Termi-nalia Chebula, (twenty-eight synonyms and seven varieties of this are enumerated; a form हरीतक is also found.)
हरिमन्त: हरिमन्त हरिमन्त, अस्, m., N. of an Āṅgirasa (author of the hymn Ṛg-veda IX. 72).
हरिले: हरिले हरिले, ind. (according to some) a vocative particle used in addressing a female slave (in theatrical language).
हरिष: हरिष हरिष, अस्, m. (a modern form of हर्ष), joy, happiness (according to Śabda-k.).
हरीषा: हरीषा हरीषा, f. a particular kind of seasoning or condiment.
हरेणु: हरेणु हरेणु, उस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. II. 1. fr. rt. 1. हृ), pease, pulse; a creeper marking the boundary of a village; N. of Laṅkā; (उस्), f. a sort of drug or perfume (= रेणुका, q. v.); a re-spectable woman; a copper-coloured deer.
हरेणुक: हरेणुक, अस्, m. pease, pulse (= कलाय).
हर्तव्य: हर्तव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be taken or accepted, to be seized, &c.
हर्मन्: हर्मन् हर्मन्, आ, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. हृ), gaping, yawning.
हर्मित: हर्मित, अस्, आ, अम्, yawned; thrown, cast, sent; burned [cf. घर्म].
हर्मुट: हर्मुट हर्मुट, अस्, m. (according to some) the sun; a tortoise.
हर्म्य: हर्म्य हर्म्य, अम्, n. (said to be fr. rt. 1. हृ in the sense of ‘to captivate or charm the mind;’ but more probably to be connected with घर्म), a hole in the ground for cooking, a kind of pit or oven for holding fire, fire-place, hearth; a domestic hearth, home; house, building, palace, mansion, any large building or residence of a man of wealth, [cf. Zend zairimya; Lat. formus]; a fiery pit, place of torment, region of darkness, abode of evil spirits, abode of the departed, the nether world; (अस्, आ, अम्), living in houses. —हर्म्य-पृष्ठ, अम्, n. the roof or upper room of a palace. —हर्म्य-भाज्, क्, क्, क्, living in a palace. —हर्म्य-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. standing near a hearth or fire-place; being in a house. —हर्म्य-स्थल, अम्, n. the room or chamber of a mansion or palace. —हर्-म्याङ्गन (°य-अङ्°), अम्, n. the court of a palace.
हर्य्: हर्य् हर्य्, cl. 1. P. हर्यति (sometimes also A. -ते), जहर्य, हर्यिष्यति, अहर्-यीत्, हर्यितुम्, Ved. to desire, yearn after, love, like, be pleased with, (in Naigh. II. 6. enumerated among the कान्ति-कर्माणः); to worship, pray to; to take [cf. rt. 1. हृ]; to threaten; to be weary; to go, (in Naigh. II. 14. enumerated among the गति-कर्माणः): Caus. हर्ययति, -यितुम्, Aor. अज-हर्यत्: Desid. जिहर्यिषति: Intens. जाहर्यते, जाहर्यीति, जाहर्ति; [cf. Gr. χαίρω, χαρ-ά, χάρ-μα, χάρι-ς, χαρίζομαι, χαρί-εις, γέλως, γελάω: Lat. gra-tu-s, grat-ia (Osc. her-est, Herentati-s, ‘Ve-nus:’ Umbr. heriest): Goth. faihu-gair-n-s, ‘ava-ricious;’ gair-uni, ‘affection;’ gailjan, gôljan: Old Germ. ger, giri, ‘desirous;’ geri, giri, ‘greedi-ness;’ gerôn, ‘to desire:’ Angl. Sax. gal, gagol: Lith. gor-u-ti, gor (?) : Slav. zel-e-ti (?) .]
हर्यत्: हर्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. desiring, liking, lov-ing, (Sāy. = कामयमान; in Ṛg-veda I. 57, 2. according to Sāy. हर्यतः = प्रेप्सतः or शोभ-नः, see the next.)
हर्यत: हर्यत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. amiable, beloved, (Sāy. = स्पृहणीय, Ṛg-veda III. 5, 3); agreeable, pleasant, delicious (said of Soma); (अस्), m. a horse; a steed fit for the Aśva-medha sacrifice; N. of the author of a hymn in the Ṛg-veda, (see प्रागाथ।)
हर्यमाण: हर्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. desiring, wishing, loving, (Sāy. = कामयमान।)
हर्ष: हर्ष, अस्, m. bristling, erection (especially of the hair, but also said of other things); thrilling, thrill, rapture, delight, glee, joy, pleasure, gladness, exultation, happiness; Joy (personified as a son of Dharma); N. of a king of Kaśmīra (celebrated as a great patron of learning; he was son of Hīra and was said to be himself a writer and poet, author of the Khaṇḍana-khaṇḍa-khādya, the Chanda-praśasti, the Nāgānanda-nāṭaka, the Naiṣadīya-carita, the Ratnāvalī, &c.); (अस्, आ, अम्), happy, delighted. —हर्ष-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, causing delight, grati-fying, delighting. —हर्ष-कीर्त्ति, इस्, m., N. of the author of a commentary on the Śruta-bodha. —हर्ष-क्रोध, औ, m. du. joy and anger. —हर्-ष-चरित, अम्, n., N. of a poem. —हर्ष-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, arising from joy. —हर्ष-जड, अस्, आ, अम्, paralyzed with joy. —हर्ष-देव, अस्, m. king Harṣa, (see हर्ष above.) —हर्ष-युक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, filled with joy, joyful. —हर्ष-वर्धन, अस्, m. ‘joy-promoter,’ N. of a king. —हर्ष-विवर्-धन, अस्, ई, अम्, increasing or promoting joy. —हर्ष-विवृद्ध-सत्त्व, अस्, आ, अम्, one whose vigour is increased by happiness. —हर्ष-विह्वल, अस्, आ, अम्, agitated with joy, overjoyed. —हर्ष-समन्वित, अस्, आ, अम्, filled with joy. —हर्ष-स्वन, अस्, m. a cry of joy, sound of pleasure. —हर्षान्वित (°ष-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, full of joy, happy. —हर्षाविष्ट (°ष-आव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, penetrated or filled with joy. —हर्षोत्कर्ष (°ष-उत्°), अस्, m. excess of happiness. —हर्षो-दय (°ष-उद्°), अस्, m. rise of joy, occurrence of pleasure.
हर्षण: हर्षण, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, causing delight, de-lighting, gladdening, delightful, pleasurable, pleasant; (अस्), m. who or what delights or rejoices; ‘glad-dener,’ epithet of one of the five arrows of Kāma-deva; the fourteenth of the astronomical Yogas; a morbid affection of the eyes; a deity presiding over Śrāddhas; a kind of Śrāddha; (अम्), n. the act of delighting or making glad, pleasing, making happy; rejoicing, being happy.
हर्षीका: हर्षीका हर्षीका, f. a kind of metre.
हल्: हल् 1. हल्, cl. 1. P. हलति, जहाल, अहा-लीत्, &c., to plough, make furrows.
हल् 2. हल्, m. n. (in Pāṇini's system) a technical expression for all the consonants; any con-sonant. —हल्-अन्त, अस्, आ, अम्, ending in a con-sonant.
हल: हल, अम्, n. a plough; ugliness, deformity, = वैरूप्य; (आ), f. the earth; water; spirituous liquor, wine. —हल-धर, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, plough-holding, having a plough; (अस्), m. a ploughman; epithet of Bala-rāma (as bearing a peculiar weapon shaped like a ploughshare; cf. सीर-पाणि). —हल-भूति, इस्, f. agriculture, husbandry. —हल-भृत्, त्, त्, त्, plough-holding, possessing a plough; (त्), m. a ploughman; Bala-rāma; [cf. सीर-भृत्।] —हल-भृति, इस्, f. ploughing, agriculture, husbandry; (इस्), m., N. of a Muni (= उप-वर्ष, कृत-कोटि, अ-याचित). —हल-मुखी, f. a kind of metre. —हल-राक्ष, अम्, n. a kind of shrub (= आहुल्य). —हल-हति, इस्, f. ‘plough-striking,’ ploughing, furrowing. —हलायुध (°ल-आय्°), अस्, m. ‘plough-weaponed,’ Bala-rāma, (see above); N. of a poet (son of Dhanañ-jaya); of the author of the Brāhmaṇa-sarvasva; of the author of the Purāṇa-sarvasva; of the author of the Abhidhāna-ratnamālā lexicon.
हलय: हलय, Nom. P. हलयति, &c., to plough (= हलिं गृह्णाति, Vopa-deva XXI. 17).
हलाह: हलाह, अस्, m. a horse of a mixed or variegated colour, (also read हालाह।)
हलि: हलि, इस्, m. a large plough, ploughshare (= जित्या, Vopa-deva XXVI. 20; = वृहद्-धल, q. v.); a furrow (according to some); agriculture.
हलिन्: हलिन्, ई, m. a ploughman, agriculturist, cultivator; N. of Bala-rāma; (इनी), f. a number of ploughs; a kind of plant (= लाङ्गलिकी). —हलि-प्रिय, अस्, m. ‘dear to agriculturists,’ the Kadamba tree; (आ), f. spirituous liquor (= मदिरा).
हली: हली, f. the plant Kali-kārī, q. v.
हलीषा: हलीषा, f. (probably fr. हल + ईषा), = लाङ्ग-लीषा, the handle of a plough.
हल्य: हल्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be ploughed or tilled, arable; belonging to or proceeding from ugliness or deformity, ugly; (आ), f. a multitude of ploughs; (अम्), n. a ploughed field, arable land; ugliness; de-formity.
हलहला: हलहला हल-हला (an imitative sound), halloo, hallooing. —हलहला-शब्द, अस्, m. shout-ing Hala-halā, hallooing, shout, outcry, tumult.
हला: हला हला, f. a female friend, (see also हला under हल); (हला), ind. a vocative particle used in addressing a female friend who is an equal (in theatrical language).
हलाहल: हलाहल हलाहल, अस्, अम्, m. n. (= हाल-हल, q. v., sometimes also written हलहल, and said to be fr. rt. 1. हल्), a sort of deadly poison [cf. कालकूट at p. 226, col. 2]; (अस्), m. a kind of snake (= ब्रह्म-सर्प); a Jaina or Bauddha sage; a sort of lizard or newt.
हलीन: हलीन हलीन, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. हल्), the Teak tree (= शाक).
हलीमक: हलीमक 1. हलीमक, अम्, n. (probably con-nected with 1. हरिमन् at p. 1167, col. 2), a sort of jaundice, paleness or yellowness of skin.
हलुआण: हलुआण हलुआण or हलूआण, N. of a place.
हल्लक: हल्लक हल्लक, अम्, n. the red lotus.
हल्लन: हल्लन हल्लन, अम्, n. rolling or tossing about, rolling about in sleep.
हल्लीश: हल्लीश हल्लीश, अम्, n. one of the eighteen Upa-rūpakas or minor dramatic entertainments (de-scribed as a piece in one act, consisting chiefly of singing and dancing by one male and seven, eight, or ten female performers), a ballet; a circular dance (performed by women).
हल्लीशक: हल्लीशक, अस्, m. dancing in a ring (as performed by women).
हव: हव 1. हव, अस्, m. (fr. rt. हु), an oblation, burnt-offering, sacrifice.
हव 2. हव, अस्, अम्, m. n. (fr. rt. ह्वे), call-ing, call; invocation, prayer; order, command; challenging, defying.
हव, अस्, अम्, m. n. calling. See 2. हव, p. 1168.
हवङ्ग: हवङ्ग, अस्, m. (probably हवं + ग), eating rice and curds from a metal cup.
हवन: 1. हवन, अम्, n. the act of offering an oblation with fire; an oblation to the gods, burnt-offering, sacrifice; (ई), f. a hole made in the ground for the sacrificial fire which is to receive a burnt-oblation.  — 1. हवन-स्यद, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. hastening to a sacrifice. —हवनायुस् (°न-आय्°), उस्, m. ‘having the burnt-offering for its life,’ fire.
2. हवन, अम्, n. the act of calling, an invoca-tion; challenging to battle. —हवन-श्रुत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. listening to an invocation. —२। हवन-स्यद, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. hastening to battle.
हवनीय: हवनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be offered with fire, fit for an oblation or sacrifice, sacrificial; (अम्), n. any-thing fit for an oblation; clarified butter, ghee.
हवित्री: हवित्री, f. a hole made in the ground for holding the sacred fire for an oblation.
हविष्य: हविष्य, अम्, n. anything fit for an oblation; clarified butter; wild rice (or any similar wild grain); rice mixed with ghee; a hymn in praise of oblations (Ved). —हविष्य-भुज्, क्, क्, क्, eating clarified butter; (क्), m. fire. —हविष्यान्न (°य-अन्°), अम्, n. food fit to be eaten during certain holy days (or during the continuance of fasts and other re-ligious observances); any particularly pure food (as wheat, cow's milk, &c.). —हविष्याशिन् (°य-आश्°), ई, इनी, इ, devouring clarified butter, (Manu XI. 218); (ई), m. fire.
हविस्: हविस्, इस्, n. anything offered as an oblation with fire, clarified butter, ghee; an oblation or burnt-offering (in general); water, (in Naigh. I. 12. enu-merated among the उदक-नामानि); epithet of Śiva. —हविः-शेष, अस्, m. the residue of an obla-tion. —हविर्-अशन, अम्, n. the act of devouring clarified butter; (अस्), m. ‘consuming oblations,’ fire. —हविर्-गन्धा, f. ‘smelling like clarified butter,’ the Śamī tree. —हविर्-गेह, अम्, n. any house or chamber in which an oblation is offered, a sacrificial hall. —हविर्-दा, आस्, आस्, अम्, Ved. a giver of obla-tions, (said of Rudra, Ṛg-veda IV. 3, 7.) —हविर्-धान, अम्, n., Ved. ‘ghee-containing,’ an oblation; (ए), n. du. the two receptacles or vehicles on which the Soma and other offerings are put; (अस्), m., N. of the author of the hymns Ṛg-veda X. 11 — 13 (having the patronymic Āṅgi). —हविर्-भुज्, क्, क्, क्, eating clarified butter; (क्), m. fire; N. of the Pitṛs of the Kṣatriyas. —हविर्-भू, ऊस्, f., N. of the wife of Pulastya. —हविर्-मथि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. destroying or obstructing oblations, impeding sacrificial rites. —हविर्-मन्थ, अस्, m. a kind of plant (= ग-णिकारी). —हविर्-यज्ञ, अस्, m. a particular sacrifice, N. of the first book of the Śata-patha-Brāhmaṇa (ac-cording to the Mādhyandina-śākhā). —हविर्-यज्ञ-संस्था, f. a kind of sacrifice, (seven Havir-yajña-saṃsthās are enumerated, viz. Agny-ādheya, Agni-hotra, Darśa-pūrṇamāsau, Cāturmāsyāni, Paśu-ban-dha, Sautrāmaṇī, and Pāka-yajña.) —हविर्-याजिन्, ई, m. ‘ghee-offerer,’ a priest. —हविष्-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. performing a sacrifice. —हविष्-पङ्क्ति, इस्, m., Ved., scil. यज्ञ, a sacrifice consisting of five oblations. —हविष्-पति, इस्, m., Ved. the lord of a sacrifice. —हविष्-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessed of oblations; (अन्तस्), m. pl., N. of a class of Pitṛs (re-garded as progenitors of Kṣatriyas and as descended from Aṅgiras; Manu III. 197, 198). —हविष्य्-अन्तीय, अम्, n., N. of nineteen Vedic texts begin-ning हविष्यन्तम्, (Manu XI. 251.)
हव्य: 1. हव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, fit to be offered in oblations, (Sāy. = होतव्य); (अस्), m., N. of a son of Atri; (अम्), n. an oblation or offering to the gods (as dis-tinguished fr. कव्य, q. v.); clarified butter, ghee. —हव्य-कव्य, अम्, n. oblations both to the gods and to the spirits of deceased ancestors, (also आनि, n. pl.) —हव्य-जुष्टि, इस्, f., Ved. the favour of an oblation, an acceptable oblation, (Sāy. = हविः-सेवा।) —हव्य-दाति, इस्, f., Ved. ‘oblation-giving,’ a sacri-ficial offering; (इस्, इस्, इ), giving sacrificial offerings. —हव्य-पाक, अस्, m. an oblation (of rice, barley, &c.) cooked with butter and milk for presentation to the gods; the vessel in which such an oblation is prepared. —हव्य-वाह्, ट्, or हव्य-वाह, अस्, m. ‘oblation-bearer,’ Agni or fire. —हव्य-वाहन, अस्, ई, अम्, bearing oblations, conveying oblations; (अस्), m. fire; epithet of the ninth Kalpa; N. of a son of Śuci. —हव्य-वाहिनी, f. ‘oblation-bearer,’ N. of a goddess. —हव्य-सूद्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. flowing with oblations, affording oblations (said of cows as affording milk that yields butter for sacrificial rites). —हव्याश (°य-आश) or हव्याशन (°य-अश्°), अस्, m. ‘oblation-eater,’ fire.
2. हव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. to be invoked, (Sāy. = आह्वातव्य।)
हवस्: हवस्, अस्, n., Ved. a song of praise, hymn, prayer.
हवीमन्: हवीमन्, आ, m., Ved. invocation; challenging; battle, (Sāy. = सङ्ग्राम, Ṛg-veda VII. 83, 4.)
हवा: हवा हवा or हवाव, ind. (a term imply-ing) undoubtedly, certainly.
हस्: हस् 1. हस्, cl. 1. P. हसति, जहास, हसि-ष्यति, अहसीत्, हसितुम्, to laugh, smile; to laugh at, ridicule (with acc.); to resemble, (see हसत्): Pass. हस्यते, Aor. अहासि: Caus. हासयति, यितुम्, Aor. अजीहसत्, to cause to laugh, make laugh, provoke laughter: Desid. जिहसिषति: Intens. जा-हस्यते, जाहस्ति, to laugh immoderately; [cf. per-haps Gr. τω-θεία, τω-θάζω; probably Lat. histrio.]

2. हस्, Ved. laughter, joy; brightness, brilliance. —हस्-कर्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, Ved. causing joy or prosperity; making bright, (Sāy. = वृद्धेः कर्तृ or प्रभासक, Ṛg-veda IV. 7, 3.) —हस्-कार, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. causing brightness or radiance (said of lightning; Sāy. = दीप्ति-कर, Ṛg-veda I. 23, 12). —हस्-कृति, इस्, f., Ved. a song of praise; (इस्, इस्, इ), causing joy, (Sāy. = हास-कारिन् or हर्षस्य सूचक, Ṛg-veda VIII. 89, 6.)
हस: हस, अस्, m. laughter, laughing, a laugh; de-rision. —हसा-मुदौ, m. du., Ved. laughing and rejoicing.
हसत्: हसत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, laughing, smiling; resem-bling (i. e. smiling like, with acc., Kirāt. VIII. 44); (अन्ती), f. a portable fire-pan, small furnace, chafing-dish; Arabian jasmine; a kind of Śākinī, q. v.
हसन: हसन, अम्, n. the act of laughing, laughter, a laugh; (आ), f. laughter; a joke, subject of laughter or ridicule, (Ṛg-veda IX. 112, 4.)
हसनी: हसनी, f. a portable fire-place or chafing-dish. —हसनी-मणि, इस्, m. ‘furnace-jewel,’ fire.
हसनीय: हसनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, laughable; to be ridiculed, ridiculous.
हसन्तिका: हसन्तिका, f. (fr. हसन्ती), a portable fire-place or small furnace.
हसित: हसित, अस्, आ, अम्, laughed, laughing, smiling; expanded, blossomed, blown (as a flower); (अम्), n. laughter, jesting; smiling; the bow of Kāma (god of love).
हसितृ: हसितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who laughs, a laugher, smiler.
हसित्वा: हसित्वा, ind. having laughed, having smiled.
हस्र: हस्र, अस्, आ, अम्, smiling; stupid, ignorant, a fool.
हास: हास, अस्, m. laughing, laughter; mirth, merry-making, joy; derision. —हास-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, causing laughter, ridiculous; laughing, merry.
हास हास, हासक, &c. See p. 1168, col. 3.
हासक: हासक, अस्, m. a laugher; one who causes laughter, a buffoon, merry-andrew.
हासमान: हासमान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. laughing, being de-lighted, (Sāy. = हासं कुर्वत्, हर्ष-युक्त।)
हासिन्: हासिन्, ई, इनी, इ, laughing, smiling, making merry.
हास्य: हास्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be laughed at, laughable, ridiculous; (अम्), n. laughter, laughing, mirth (one of the ten Rasas, see रस), jest, amusement; ridi-cule, derision. —हास्य-ता, f. laughableness, ridicu-lousness. —हास्य-पदवी, f. ‘road of laughter,’ ridicule, laughter, (हास्य-पदवीं या, to expose one's self to laughter, incur ridicule.) —हास्य-रस, अस्, m. the sentiment of humour, sense of humour, comic vein, facetiousness (the fifth of the ten Rasas, see रस). —हास्यार्णव (°य-अर्°), अस्, m. ‘ocean of mirth,’ N. of a drama by Jagad-īśvara. —हास्या-स्पद (°य-आस्°), अम्, n. a laughing-stock, butt for derision.
हस्त: हस्त हस्त, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. III. 86. fr. rt. 1. हस्), the hand; the thirteenth as-terism, (see below); the fore-arm, cubit; a measure of length from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger (= twenty-four Aṅgulas or about eighteen inches); an elephant's trunk; (in prosody) an ana-pest; quantity, abundance, mass, (in this sense only at end of comps. and when compounded with words signifying ‘hair;’ cf. केश-हस्त); (आ), f. the thir-teenth lunar asterism (represented by a hand and containing five stars, identified by some with part of the constellation Corvus); (अम्), n. a pair of leather bellows; (ए), ind. in hand, in one's possession; [cf. Gr. χανδ-άν-ω (ἔ-χαδ-ον, κέ-χανδ-α, χείσομαι); Lat. pre-hend-o, hed-era (?) ; Goth. bi-git-an, handu; Angl. Sax. gitan (= Eng. get), hand.] —हस्त-कमल, अम्, n. a lotus carried in the hand (thus when Lakṣmī was churned out of the ocean, she appeared holding a lotus). —हस्त-कौ-शल, अम्, n. skilfulness of hand, manual dexterity. —हस्त-क्रिया, f. any manual performance. —हस्त-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, come to hand, fallen into one's possession, procured, gained, obtained, secured. —हस्त-गिरि, इस्, m., N. of a mountain. —हस्त-गृह्य, ind., Ved. having taken the hand. —हस्त-घ्न, अस्, m., Ved. a kind of arm-guard or shield (defending the fore-arm from the blows of the bow-string). —हस्त-चापल्य, अम्, n. = हस्त-कौशल। —हस्त-च्छेदन, अम्, n. the amputation of a hand. —हस्त-च्युत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. shaken or moved with the hand, moved or thrown violently by means of the hand. —हस्त-च्युति, इस्, f., Ved. moving or shaking about with the hand, (according to Sāy. हस्त-च्युती = हस्त-प्रच्युत्या, हस्त-गत्या, Ṛg-veda VII. 1, 1.) —हस्त-ज्योडि, इस्, m. a kind of tree or plant (= कर-ज्योडि). —हस्त-तल, अम्, n. the palm of the hand; the tip of an elephant's trunk. —हस्त-ताल, अस्, m. clapping the hands together. —हस्त-त्रय-सम्मिते, ind. at a distance of three Hastas. —हस्त-दोष, अस्, m. a slip of the hand, mistake committed by the hand. —हस्त-धात्री = हस्तामलक. —हस्त-धारण, अम्, n. warding off a blow; stopping a blow with the hand. —हस्त-पादादि (°द-आदि), the hands and feet &c., the extremities, the limbs of the body. —हस्त-पुच्छ, अम्, n. the lower part of the fore-arm, the hand below the wrist. —हस्त-पृष्ठ, अम्, n. the back of the hand (also called अप-पृष्ठ). —हस्त-प्राप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, reached with the hand, held in the hand; obtained, secured (= कर-प्राप्त)। —हस्त-मणि, इस्, m. a jewel worn on the wrist. —हस्त-मात्र, a cubit in length, (see मात्र।) —हस्त-युगल, अम्, n. the two hands. —हस्त-रत्नावली (°न-आव्°), f., N. of a work by Rāghava (treating of the various movements of the hands &c.). —हस्त-रेखा, f. a line on the hand. —हस्त-लाघव, अम्, n. lightness of hand, manual readiness, smartness, cleverness, legerdemain. —हस्त-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having hands, handy, dexterous, clever, skilful. —हस्त-वर्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, being or remain-ing in the hand, seized, held, caught hold of. —हस्त-वारण, अम्, n. restraining the hand (of another); warding off a blow. —हस्त-विम्ब, अम्, n. perfuming or smearing the body with unguents &c. —हस्त-संवाहन, अम्, n. rubbing or sham-pooing with the hands. —हस्त-सिद्धि, इस्, f. per-forming or effecting anything with the hand, manual labour; hire, wages, salary. —हस्त-सूत्र or हस्त-सूत्रक, ‘hand-ribbon;’ (अम्), n. a bracelet worn on the wrist. —हस्त-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, staying in the hand, being in hand, held, grasped. —हस्त-स्थित, अस्, आ, अम्, being in hand, held. —हस्ताक्षर (°त-अक्°), अम्, n. one's own sign manual, autograph, signature, handwriting. —हस्ताग्र (°त-अग्°), अम्, n. the extremity of the hand, the fingers. —हस्ता-ग्र-लग्न (°त-अग्°), अस्, आ, अम्, ‘joined hand in hand,’ married; [cf. पाणि-ग्रह।] —हस्ताङ्गुलि (°त-अङ्°), इस्, f. ‘hand-finger,’ any finger of the hand. —हस्तामलक (°त-आम्°), अस्, m., N. of one of the four principal disciples of Śaṅkarācārya; (अम्), n. the fruit of Emblic Myrobalan held in the hand; N. of a short work by Hastāmalaka (containing the elements of the Vedānta). —हस्तामलक-भा-ष्य, अम्, n. a commentary on the above by Śaṅ-karācārya. —हस्तावलम्ब (°त-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, supported by the hand of another. —हस्तावाप (°त-आव्°), अस्, m. ‘hand-bracelet,’ a finger-guard, arm-guard (used by archers, = ज्याघात-वारण). —हस्ता-हस्ति, ind. hand to hand. —हस्ते-करण, अम्, n. ‘taking by the hand,’ marriage (= पाणौ-करण). —हस्ते-कृ, cl. 8. हस्तक: हस्तक, अस्, m. a position of the hands.
हस्तिक: हस्तिक, अस्, n. a multitude or collection of ele-phants (= गज-त).
हस्तिन्: हस्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having hands, having a trunk; (ई), m. an elephant, (four kinds of elephants are specified, each characterized by particular marks; see भद्र, मन्द्र, मृग, मिश्र; some give कि-लिञ्ज-हस्तिन्, a traw elephant, effigy of an elephant made of grass); N. of a son of king Su-hotra (a prince of the Lunar race, described in Viṣṇu-Purāṇa IV. 19. as founder of Hastinā-pura); a kind of plant, = अज-मोदा; (इनी), f. a female elephant; a woman of a particular class (one of the four into which females are divided; a woman of this class is de-scribed as having thick lips, thick hips, thick fingers, large breasts, dark complexion, and libidinous ap-petite); a kind of drug and perfume. —हस्ति-कक्-ष्य, अस्, m. a lion; a tiger. —हस्ति-कन्द, अस्, m. a kind of tree or bulbous plant (described as a sort of Arum, = गज-कन्द). —हस्ति-करञ्ज, अस्, m. a kind of tree (= महा-करञ्ज). —हस्ति-कर्ण, अस्, m. ‘elephant-eared,’ the castor-oil tree (also the red kind); a kind of Palāśa tree; another tree or bulbous plant (= हस्ति-कन्द); a particular class of semi-divine beings (forming one of the गण-देवता, q. v.); N. of a district. —हस्ति-कर्णक, अस्, m. a kind of Palāśa tree. —हस्तिकर्ण-दल, अस्, m. a sort of Palāśa tree. —हस्ति-कोलि, इस्, m. a sort of jujube. —हस्ति-गिरि, इस्, m. the city and district of Kāñcī, q. v. —हस्ति-घट, N. of the seventh book of the Śata-patha-Brāhmaṇa. —हस्ति-घोषा or हस्ति-घोषातकी, f. a kind of creeper (= ऐभी, महा-कोशातकी). —हस्ति-घ्न, अस्, m. an elephant-killer; a man. —हस्ति-चारिन्, ई, m. an elephant-driver; (इणी), f. a kind of tree (= महा-करञ्ज)। —हस्ति-दन्त, अस्, m. the tusk of an elephant; a radish; a pin or peg projecting from a wall; (अम्), n. ivory; a radish. —हस्ति-दन्तक, अम्, n. a radish. —हस्तिदन्त-फला, f. a kind of cucumber (= एर्वारु). —हस्ति-द्वयस, अस्, ई, अम् (Gram. 80. XX), as high or as big as an elephant, elephantine. —हस्ति-नख, अम्, n. ‘elephant's nail,’ a sort of turret or raised mound of earth or masonry protecting the access to the gate of a city or fort, (it is described as furnished with an inner staircase, and affording means for discharging arrows &c. at an enemy.) —हस्ति-प or हस्तिपक, अस्, m. an elephant-driver, ele-phant-rider; an elephant-keeper. —हस्ति-पत्त्र, अस्, m. = हस्ति-कन्द. —हस्ति-पर्णिका, f. a kind of plant (= राज-कोशातकी). —हस्ति-पर्णी, f. a kind of plant (= मोरटा); a sort of gourd (= कर्-कटी). —हस्ति-पाद, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, elephant-footed. —हस्ति-पाल, अस्, m., N. of a king. —हस्ति-पृष्ठक, अम्, n. the back of an elephant. —हस्ति-मद, अस्, m. the ichor or exudation from an elephant's temples when in rut. —हस्ति-मल्ल, अस्, m., N. of Airāvata (Indra's elephant); of Ga-ṇeśa; of Śaṅkha (the eighth of the chief Nāgas or serpents of Pātāla); a heap of ashes; a shower of dust; frost, cold. —हस्ति-मात्र, अस्, ई, अम्, as great as an elephant. —हस्ति-यूथ, अम्, n. a herd of elephants. —हस्ति-राज, अस्, m. the king or chief of elephants. —हस्ति-रोहणक, अस्, m. a kind of tree (= महा-करञ्ज). —हस्ति-लोध्रक, अस्, m. the Lodhra tree. —हस्ति-वध or हस्ति-बध, अस्, m. the killing of an elephant (especially by a lion, which incurs the guilt of murder, whilst others carry off the spoils, such as the tusks and the pearls said to be found in the head). —हस्ति-वर्चस, अम्, n. the magnificence of an elephant. —हस्ति-वाह, अस्, m. an elephant-driver; a hook for driving elephants. —हस्ति-विषाणी, f. the Kadalī tree. —हस्ति-वै-द्यक, N. of a work by Vīra-soma. —हस्ति-शाला, f. an elephant-stable. —हस्ति-शुण्ड, अस्, m. or हस्ति-शुण्डा, f. an elephant's trunk; (आ or ई), f. the shrub Heliotropium Indicum. —हस्ति-श्या-माक, अस्, m. a kind of grain. —हस्ति-षड्गव, अम्, n. a yoke or collection of six elephants, (see षड्-गव।) —हस्ति-सोमा, f., N. of a river. —हस्ति-स्नान, अम्, n. the washing of an ele-phant. —हस्ति-हस्त, अस्, m. an elephant's trunk. —हस्ति-हस्त-परामृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, touched or struck by the trunks of elephants. —हस्त्य्-अध्य्-अक्ष, अस्, m. a superintendent or master of ele-phants. —हस्त्य्-अश्व-रथ-सम्बाध, अस्, आ, अम्, crowded with carriages, horses, and elephants. —हस्त्य्-आयुर्वेद, अस्, m. a work on the treat-ment of elephants' diseases. —हस्त्य्-आरोह, अस्, m. an elephant-rider, elephant-driver.
हस्तिनपुर: हस्तिन-पुर, अम्, n. (fr. हस्तिन् + पुर), the city of Hastin (= हस्तिना-पुर below).
हस्तिनापुर: हस्तिना-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a city founded by king Hastin, q. v., (it was situated about fifty-seven miles north-east of the modern Dillī or Delhi on the banks of an old channel of the Ganges, and was the capital of the kings of the Lunar line, as Ayodhyā was of the Solar dynasty; hence it forms a central scene of action in the Mahā-bhārata; here Dhṛta-rāṣṭra reigned when the government was resigned by his brother Pāṇḍu, and here the five Pāṇḍava princes were educated along with their cousins the Kauravas, and here at the conclusion of the great war between them Yudhi-ṣṭhira was crowned after a triumphal progress through the streets of the city; see Śānti-parvan 1386-1410: other names for this celebrated town are गजाह्वय, नाग-साह्वय, नागाह्व, हास्तिन।)
हस्त्य: हस्त्य, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to the hand, done with the hand, manual; given with the hand.
हहल: हहल हहल, अम्, n. (= हाहल, see हाल-हल), a sort of deadly poison.
हहा: हहा हहा, आस्, m. a kind of Gandharva, q. v.; [cf. 1. हाहा, हुहू।]
हा: हा 1. हा, ind. an exclamation of pain or grief or weariness (equivalent to ‘ah!’ ‘alas!’ ‘woe!’ हा हतो ऽस्मि, ah! I am killed! it is all over with me); an exclamation of joy or surprise (oh! ha! &c.); an interjection of anger or reproach; [cf. 2. हाहा।]

A. जिहीते (1st sing. जिहे, 3rd du. जिहाते, 2nd pl. जिहीध्वे, 3rd pl. जिहते), Impf. अजिहीत, Pot. जिहीत, Impv. जिहीताम्, Perf. जहे, हास्यते, अहास्त, हातुम्, to go, move, to go to, attain; to give way, yield [cf. Gr. χα-ίν-ω, χά-σκ-ω, χάσμα, χά-ος, χή-μη, χάσις, χαλάω; Lat. hi-sc-o, hi-o, hia-tus; Old Germ. gî-ê-m, gin-ê-m, gein-o-m; Angl. हा 3. हा (connected with rt. 2. हा), cl. 3. P. जहाति (1st du. जहीवस् or जहिवस्, 3rd du. जहीतस् or जहितस्, 3rd. pl. जहति, Pāṇ. VI. 4, 116), Impf. अजहात् (1st du. अजहीव or अजहिव, 3rd pl. अजहुः), Pot. जह्यात् (Pāṇ. VI. 4, 118), Impv. जहातु (2nd sing. जहीहि or जहिहि or जहाहि, 3rd pl. जहतु, Pāṇ. VI. 4, 117), Perf. जहौ (2nd sing. जहिथ or जहाथ, 1st du. ज-हिव, 2nd pl. जह, 3rd pl. जहुः), हास्यति, अहासीत्, Prec. हेयात्, हातुम्, to abandon, leave, quit, desert, forsake, relinquish, dismiss; to resign, forego, let go, lose; to let fall; to omit, neglect; to avoid, shun; to remove: Pass. हीयते, Perf. जहे (Kirāt. हात्वा: हात्वा, ind. (Pāṇ. VII. 4, 43), having gone, hav-ing moved.
हान: हान, अस्, आ, अम्, gone, moved.
हान, अम्, n. the act of abandoning, relinquish-ing; escaping; prowess, valour.
हास्यमान: हास्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being about to go.

हेय हेय। See under rts. 2. 3. हा, 1. हि।
हातव्य: हातव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be abandoned or left, relinquishable.
हानि: हानि, इस्, f. abandonment, relinquishment, neglect, loss, want, privation, absence; decrease, deficiency, diminution, detriment, damage. —हानि-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, causing loss, prejudicial, injurious.
हापन: हापन, अम्, n. the act of causing to quit or abandon, expelling.
हापित: हापित, अस्, आ, अम्, caused to be relinquished; made to give up.

P. जिहर्ति; in Śatapatha-Brāhmaṇa X. 4, 3, 9. there is a form हरासै, ‘thou may'st have seized’), हर्तुम्, to bring, convey, carry, fetch; to carry away, carry off, take away, take off, seize, take hold of, extricate; to rob, plunder, steal; to strip off, spoil, despoil, remove, deprive of; to take, acquire, gain, obtain, hold; to captivate, charm; to accept, receive, inherit; to throw, cast (an arrow &c.); to offer: Pass. ह्रियते, Aor. अहारि, to be taken or seized, &c.: Caus. हारयति, -ते, -यितुम्, Aor. अजीहरत्, -त, to cause to bring or carry or seize (with acc. and inst. or with a double acc.), cause to take or take hold of; to give, give away; to permit to be carried off or plundered; to send: Desid. जिहीर्षति, -ते, to wish to take or carry off, wish to rob, &c.: Intens. जेह्रीयते, जर्हरीति, जरिहरीति, जरीहरीति, जर्-हर्ति, जरिहर्ति, जरीहर्ति; [cf. Zend zar; Gr. χείρ, εὐ-χερ-ής, χέρ-ης, χράομαι, κίχρημι, (accord-ing to some also perhaps) αἴρω, αἱρέω (for χαίρω), ἀγείρω; Old Lat. hir; Lat. heru-s, hera, her-e(d)-s, (perhaps also) co-hors, (according to some also per-haps) gero; Goth. geiro, gairon, gairnjan; Angl. Sax. georu, geornian; Eng. yare.]

हृ 2. हृ or हॄ (referred in native lists to the Nom. हृणीय below, technically called हृणीङ्, but connected with rt. 1. ह्री, q. v., and perhaps better written हॄ), cl. 9. A. हृणीते, &c., Ved. originally perhaps ‘to be yellow’ (cf. हरि); to blush; to be ashamed, (Sāy. लज्जायाम्); to be angry (रोषायाम्), be displeased, (Sāy. हृणीते = क्रुध्यति, Ṛg-veda VII. 86, 3; हृणीषे = क्रु-ध्यसि, Ṛg-veda VII. 104, 14.)
हरक: हरक, अस्, m. a conveyer, taker; a seizer; N. of Śiva; a thief, rogue, cheat; (in arithmetic) a divisor; division; a reflecting or judicious person (according to some).
हरणीय: हरणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be taken or accepted, acceptable; to be taken away or seized; to be divided.
हरत्: हरत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, conveying, taking away, seizing, &c.
हरस्: हरस्, अस्, n., Ved. anger, (Sāy. = क्रोध; cf. Naigh. II. 13); flame, heat, warmth, (enumerated among the ज्वलतो नामधेयानि, Naigh. I. 17); impetuosity, precipitation; day; water; blood; the world, (see Nirukta IV. 19.) —हरस्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. impetuous, precipitate, (Sāy. = वेग-वत्); (अती), f., Ved. a river, (in Naigh. I. 13. हरस्व-त्यः is enumerated among the नदी-नामानि।)
हर्तृ: हर्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who brings or conveys, one who takes or receives, a taker, receiver, seizer; a robber; taking up, absorbing; (ता), m. the sun (= सूर्य).
हारक: हारक, अस्, इका, अम्, bringing; taking, seizing; (अस्), m. one who seizes or takes away, a plunderer, thief; a cheat, rogue; a gambler; a kind of prose composition; a particular science; the tree Trophis Aspera; (in arithmetic) a divisor; a string of pearls.
हारयिष्यत्: हारयिष्यत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, about to con-vey or transmit.
हारियोजन: हारियोजन, अस्, m. (see हरि-योजन), ‘har-nesser of the Hari steeds,’ Indra; a particular Graha or portion of an offering taken out of the Āgrayaṇa libation.
हारी: हारी, f. a pearl, (see हार above.)
हृत्: हृत्, त्, त्, त् (at the end of comps.), taking away, removing, carrying off, seizing, &c.
हृत: हृत, अस्, आ, अम्, taken, taken away, seized; captivated; accepted; (अम्), n. that which is taken; a portion, share. —हृत-चन्द्र, अस्, आ, अम्, having the moon taken away; destitute of moon, moon-less. —हृत-ज्ञान, अस्, आ, अम्, bereft of knowledge, void of knowledge. —हृत-द्रव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, stripped of everything, deprived of one's property. —हृत-धन, अस्, आ, अम्, spoiled of wealth. —हृत-प्रसाद, अस्, आ, अम्, deprived of calmness. —हृत-मानस, अस्, आ, अम्, deprived of mind, robbed of one's senses. —हृत-राज्य, अस्, आ, अम्, stripped of a kingdom. —हृत-वासस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, whose dress is taken away, deprived of clothes. —हृत-सर्वस्व, अस्, आ, अम्, robbed or stripped of all personal property, entirely ruined. —हृता-धिकार (°त-अध्°), अस्, आ, अम्, deprived of an office, turned out; deprived of one's right. —हृ-तोत्तर (°त-उत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, deprived of an answer, left without a reply. —हृतोत्तरीय (°त-उत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having the upper garments stripped off. —हृतोरग (°त-उर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, deprived or devoid of snakes.
हृति: हृति, इस्, f. taking away, seizure, robbing, rob-bery; destruction.
हृत्वा: हृत्वा, ind. having taken or seized, having ac-cepted, &c.
ह्रियमाण: ह्रियमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being taken or seized; being captivated or attracted.
हृणान: हृणान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. angry, irate, displeased, (Sāy. = हृणीयमान, Ṛg-veda I. 25, 2.)
हृणि: हृणि, इस्, m., Ved. anger (= क्रोध, Naigh. II. 13); flaming, (in Naigh. I. 17. enumerated among the ज्वलतो नामधेयानि।)
हृणीय: हृणीय, Nom. A. हृणीयते, &c., to be angry; to be ashamed; [cf. Gr. χολή; Lat. fel, bilis; Old Germ. galla; Angl. Sax. gealla.]
हृणीयमान: हृणीयमान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. being angry.
हृणीया: हृणीया, f. censure, reproach; shame, bashfulness.
हृद्: हृद् हृद्, त्, n. (abbreviated fr. हर्द्, but said by some to be connected with rt. 1. हृ; it is defective in declension, being optionally substi-tuted for हृदय in all cases except the first five inflections or Nom. sing. du. pl., Acc. sing. du.; it is said by some to be also masc.), the heart; the mind, (हृद्य् अवेदिन्, ‘one who has no knowledge or capacity of knowledge in the mind,’ applied to animals), the soul, the faculty or seat of thought and feeling; the interior of the body, breast, chest, bosom; the interior or essence of anything; [cf. Gr. κῆρ, κέαρ, καρδ-ία, κραδ-ίη; Lat. cor (cord-is), dimin. cor-culum, cordatus, vêcors; Goth. hairt-o; Old Germ. herza; Mod. Germ. Herz; Angl. Sax. heorte; Eng. heart; Lith. szird-i-s; Slav. srŭ-dĭce.] —हृच्-छय, अस्, आ, अम् (i. e. हृद् + शय), lying or abiding in the heart; (अस्), m. ‘heart-dweller,’ epithet of Kāma-deva (god of love), love. —हृच्छय-पीडित, अस्, आ, अम्, tormented by love, love-sick. —हृच्छय-वर्धन, अस्, ई, अम्, aug-menting love. —हृच्छयाविष्ट-चेतन (°य-आव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having a heart penetrated by love. —हृच्-छूल, अम्, n. (i. e. हृद् + शूल), ‘heart-pang,’ any acute internal pain, pain in the chest. —हृच्-छोक, अस्, m. (i. e. हृद् + शोक), heart-ache; a pang. —हृत्-कम्प, अस्, m. heart-throb, tremor of the heart, palpita-tion. —हृत्-पिण्ड, अम्, n. ‘heart-mass,’ the heart. —हृत्-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, being in the heart, seated in the heart. —हृत्स्व्-अस्, अस्, अस्, अस्, Ved. throwing into the heart. —हृदं-सनि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. giving the heart; receiving the heart or essence of anything; receiving affection or kindness. —हृद्-आवर्त, अस्, m. a curl or lock of hair on a horse's chest. —हृदि-स्पृश्, क्, क्, क्, ‘touching or lying in the heart,’ dear, beloved, cherished. —हृद्-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, gone to the heart, seated in the heart or mind, come to mind, conceived, designed; cherished; (अम्), n. anything fixed in the mind, design, meaning, intent. —हृद्-गोल, अस्, m., N. of a mountainous district. —हृद्गोलीय, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to the above district; (आस्), m. pl. the inhabitants of the Hṛd-gola mountains. —हृद्-ग्रह, अस्, m. ‘heart-seizure,’ spasm of the heart. —हृद्-ग्रन्थ, अस्, m. (accord-ing to Śabda-k.) a heart-wound, heart-sore (= हृद्-व्रण). —हृद्-देश, अस्, m. the region of the heart. —हृद्-भेद-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a Tan-tra work. —हृद्-रुज्, क्, f. ‘heart-disease,’ grief. —हृद्-रोग, अस्, m. heart-disease, heart-ache, heart-burn; sorrow, grief, anguish; love; the zodiacal sign Aquarius. —हृद्रोग-वैरिन्, ई, m. ‘hostile to heart-burn,’ the tree Pentaptera Arjuna. —हृद्-वण्टक, अस्, m. ‘partitioning the heart or chest,’ the stomach. —हृल्-लास, अस्, m. ‘heart-sport,’ hiccough; heart-disturbance, disquietude, grief. —हृल्-लेख, अस्, m. ‘heart-impression,’ knowledge, reasoning; ‘heart-scratch,’ heart-ache, heart-sorrow; (आ), f. disquietude, anxiety or regret for any absent object.
हृदय: हृदय, अम्, n. the mind, soul, seat or faculty of thought and feeling, (चपल-हृदय, fickle-minded); affection, love; the heart; the interior of the body, breast, chest, bosom; the interior or centre or essence of anything; true or divine knowledge; the Veda; science; [cf. Gr. καρδία, &c.; Hib. croi-dhe, cridhe, ‘the heart.’] —हृदय-कम्प, अस्, m. tremor or throb of the heart, palpitation. —हृ-दय-कम्पन, अम्, n. throbbing of the heart; (अस्, ई, अम्), heart-stirring, heart-agitating, causing the heart to throb (with indignation &c.). —हृ-दय-ग्रन्थि, इस्, m. ‘heart-tie, heart-bond,’ any-thing which binds the soul. —हृदय-ग्राहिन्, ई, इणी, इ, heart-captivating, engaging the affection. —हृदयङ्-गम, अस्, आ, अम्, going to the heart, heart-stirring, thrilling, affecting, touching, moving, dear, beloved; (अम्), n. an apposite or appropriate speech. —हृदय-चौर, अस्, m. a heart-robber, one who steals the heart or affections. —हृदय-च्छिद्, त्, त्, त्, heart-breaking, heart-piercing, heart-rending. —हृदय-दौर्बल्य, अम्, n. weakness of heart, faintheartedness. —हृदय-रज्जु, (in geometry) a central line, the semidiameter of a circle in contact with the angles of a trapezium. —हृदय-लेख, अस्, m. heart-impression, knowledge; ‘heart-scratch,’ heart-ache, anxiety, (see हृल्-लेख।) —हृ-दय-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a heart, tender-hearted, kind, humane. —हृदय-विध्, त्, त्, त् (विध् for व्यध्, see rt. 2. विध्), heart-piercing. —हृदय-वृत्ति, इस्, f. disposition or inclination of the heart. —हृदय-वेधिन्, ई, इनी, इ, heart-piercing, piercing the vitals (said of an arrow). —हृदय-शल्य, अम्, n. a dagger or arrow in the heart, wound in the heart. —हृदय-शोक, अस्, m. heart-sorrow, heart-ache, a pang of grief. —हृदय-शोषण, अस्, ई, अम्, heart-withering. —हृदय-सन्निहित, अस्, आ, अम्, placed or deposited in the heart, fixed or laid up in the mind. —हृदय-सम्मित, अस्, आ, अम्, breast-high, as high as the breast. —हृदय-साहि, इस्, m. a proper N. —हृदय-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, being in the heart, cherished in the heart. —हृदय-स्थान, अम्, n. ‘seat of the heart,’ the breast, chest, bosom. —हृदयात्मन् (°य-आत्°), आ, m. a heron. —हृ-दयामय (°य-आम्°), अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having sick-ness of heart, heart-sickening. —हृदयाम्बुज (°य-अम्°), अम्, n. ‘heart-lotus,’ a lotus-like heart. —हृदयाविध् (°य-आव्°), त्, त्, त्, heart-piercing. —हृदयेश (°य-ईश) or हृदयेश्वर (°य-ईश्°), अस्, m. ‘heart-lord,’ a husband; (आ), f. ‘heart-mistress,’ a wife; a mistress. —हृदयोदङ्क (°य-उद्°), अस्, m. upheaving or torturing the heart; (अस्, आ, अम्), heart heaving, heart-disturbing.
हृदयालु: हृदयालु, उस्, उस्, उ, good-hearted, tender-hearted, affectionate, friendly.
हृदयावी: हृदयावी, (according to some) Ved. one who has a heart.
हृदयिक: हृदयिक, अस्, आ, अम्, good-hearted, tender-hearted.
हृदयिन्: हृदयिन्, ई, इनी, इ, good-hearted, tender-hearted.
हृदीक: हृदीक, अस्, m., N. of a Yādava king.
हृद्य: हृद्य, अस्, आ, अम्, hearty, cordial, proceeding from or produced in the heart; dear to the heart, beloved, cherished, desired; affectionate, kind; grate-ful, pleasant, agreeable; savory; (अस्), m. a Vedic Mantra employed to effect the subjection or fascina-tion of an enemy or rival; (आ), f. the medicinal root called Vṛddhi; (अम्), n. the bank of the Laurus Cassia. —हृद्य-गन्ध, अस्, m. the Vilva tree; (आ), f. great-flowered jasmine; (अम्), n. small cumin; sochal salt. —हृद्य-गन्धि, n. small cumin. —हृद्य-ता, f. or हृद्य-त्व, अम्, n. cordiality, heartiness, agreeableness, delightfulness.
हृष्: हृष् हृष् (originally भृष्), cl. 4. 1. P. हृष्यति, हर्षति (ep. also A. -ते), ज-हर्ष, हर्षिष्यति, अहृषत्, अहर्षीत्, हर्-षितुम्, to bristle or become erect (as the hair of the body); to thrill with rapture, rejoice, exult, be glad or pleased; to become erect (said of other things besides the hair); (according to some, also) to speak or affirm falsely, lie (but in this sense only P.): Pass. हृष्यते, Aor. अहर्षि: Caus. हर्षयति, -यि-तुम्, Aor. अजहर्षत् or अजीहृषत्, to make glad, cause to rejoice; to be glad, rejoice: Desid. जिहर्-षिषति: Intens. जरीहृष्यते, जर्हर्ष्टि, &c., to rejoice very much, be exceedingly elated; [cf. Gr. φρίσσω, φρίξ, (perhaps also) χέρσος, χήρ; Lat. horreo, Hersilia; Old Germ. burst; Angl. Sax. byrst, bristl, forst, frost, frysan, a-grisan, gerst, gryre.]
हर्षक: हर्षक, अस्, आ or इका, अम्, delighting, gladden-ing, rejoicing, pleasing, delightful; (अस्), m., N. of a particular mountain; of a king belonging to the Śaiśunāga dynasty.
हर्षमाण: हर्षमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, rejoicing, joyful, cheer-ful, happy.
हर्षयत्: हर्षयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, causing to rejoice, glad-dening.
हर्षयित्नु: हर्षयित्नु, उस्, उस्, उ, gladdening, causing de-light, delighting; (उस्), m. a son, child; (उ), n. gold.
हर्षाय: हर्षाय, Nom. A. हर्षायते, &c., to be glad.
हर्षित: हर्षित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Caus.), made glad or happy, gladdened, delighted, happy.
हर्षिन्: हर्षिन्, ई, इणी, इ, rejoicing, delighting; (इणी), f. a particular plant (= वि-जया).
हर्षु: हर्षु, Ved. joy, delight. —हर्षु-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. delighted, exulting; eager for war, (Sāy. = हर्ष-युक्त, i. e. सङ्ग्रामोत्सुक, Ṛg-veda VIII. 16, 4.)
हर्षुल: हर्षुल, अस्, आ, अम्, disposed to be cheerful or happy, delighted; (अस्), m. a deer; a lover.
हृषि: हृषि, (probably) rejoicing; (ई), m. du. Agni and Soma, (according to Śabda-k. = अग्नी-सोमौ।) —हृषी-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. full of joy, glad, happy, (Sāy. = प्राप्त-हर्ष, Ṛg-veda II. 31, 1.)
हृषित: हृषित, अस्, आ, अम्, having the hair bristling or thrilling (with joy &c.); enraptured, delighted, pleased; astonished, surprised; erect, fresh (as flowers, opposed to म्लान); disappointed, deceived; bent, bowed (= प्र-णत); armed, accoutred (= वर्-मित). —हृषित-स्रज्, क्, क्, क्, having a fresh gar-land (the flowers of which are erect and unfaded).
हृषीक: हृषीक, अम्, n. any organ of sense (= इन्द्रिय)। —हृषीकेश (°क-ईश), अस्, m. ‘lord of the organs of sense,’ Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa. —हृषीकेश-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
हृष्ट: हृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम् [cf. हृषित], having the hair of the body bristling or thrilling (with delight or rapture), enraptured, delighted, rejoiced, pleased, glad, joyous, delighted; exulting, laughing, smiling; astonished, surprised; disappointed, deceived (= प्रति-हत). —हृष्ट-चित्त, अस्, आ, अम्, rejoiced in heart. —हृष्ट-पुष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, merry and fat, happy and well-fed. —हृष्ट-पुष्टाङ्ग (°ट-अङ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, merry and fat in limb, happy and well nourished, frisky and fat. —हृष्ट-मानस, अस्, ई, अम्, rejoiced in mind, glad in heart, happy. —हृष्ट-रूप, अस्, आ, अम्, thrilling with happi-ness, in a happy or cheerful mood. —हृष्ट-रोमन्, आ, आ, अ, having the hair of the body bristling or thrilling (with delight or rapture). —हृष्ट-वत्, ind. cheerfully. —हृष्ट-वदन, अस्, आ, अम्, merry-faced, having a cheerful countenance. —हृ-ष्ट-सङ्कल्प, अस्, आ, अम्, pleased in mind, con-tented, glad. —हृष्ट-हृदय, अस्, आ, अम्, joyous-hearted, light-hearted, happy.
हृष्टि: हृष्टि, इस्, f. delight, pleasure, joy, happiness; pride, arrogance.
हृष्ट्वा: हृष्ट्वा, ind. having rejoiced, being delighted.
हे: हे हे, ind. a vocative particle (oh! ho! &c.); a particle used in vociferating or challenging (hallo! ho there!); an interjection expressing envy or ill-will or disapprobation.
हेक्का: हेक्का हेक्का, f. (fr. rt. हिक्क्), hiccough.
हेठ्: हेठ् हेठ् (according to some written हेट्), cl. 1. A. P. हेठते, हेठति (according to some हेटति), जिहेठे, हेठितुम्, to be wicked; to vex, harass, obstruct; to strike, hurt, injure; cl. 9. P. हेठ्नाति, &c. = rt. हेढ्: Caus. हेठयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अजिहेठत्।
हेठ: हेठ, अस्, m. vexation, harassing; hindering, preventing, hindrance, obstruction, opposition; in-jury, hurt.
हेड्: हेड् हेड् or (in the Veda) हेल् or हेऌ (see rt. हेल्), cl. 1. A. हेडते (Ved. हेलते, हे-ऌअते), जिहेडे, हेडितुम्, to disregard, slight, neglect; to be displeased or angry (Ved.; हेऌअते = क्रुध्यति, Naigh. II. 12); cl. 1. P. हेडति, जिहेड, &c., to surround, clothe, attire: Pass. हेड्यते, Aor. अहिडि or अहीडि or अहेडि, to be surrounded or attired: Caus. हेडयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अजिहेडत्, to cause to disregard, &c.; हिडयति, -यितुम्, अजीहिडत्, to cause to surround.
हेड: हेड, अस्, m. disregard, slight. —हेड-ज, अस्, m. passion, anger, displeasure.
हेडमान: हेडमान, अस्, आ, अम्, disregarding, neglecting, neglectful.
हेडस्: हेडस्, अस्, n., Ved. anger, wrath, (Sāy. = क्रोध।)
हेळस्: हेऌअस्, अस्, n., Ved. = हेडस् above.
हेडावुक्क: हेडावुक्क हेडावुक्क, अस्, m. (= हेलावुक्क, q. v.), a horse-dealer, horse-seller.
हेढ्: हेढ् हेढ् (also written हेठ्), cl. 9. P. हेढ्नाति, &c., to be born again; to pro-duce happiness, cause prosperity; to purify [cf. rts. खच्, खव्].
हेम: हेम, अम्, n. (abbreviated fr. 2. हेमन्, col. 1), gold; (अस्), m. a horse of a dark or brownish colour [cf. हरिय, p. 1167]; a particular weight of gold (= माषक); N. of the father of Su-tapas; of a king; = हेम-चन्द्र, q. v.; (आ), f. a handsome woman; an Apsaras of Indra's heaven; N. of a river.
हेमल: हेमल, अस्, m. a goldsmith; a chameleon, lizard; the touchstone.
हेम्य: हेम्य, अस्, आ, अम्, golden, made of gold. —हे-म्या-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having golden trappings, (Sāy. = सुवर्ण-निर्मित-कक्ष्यावत्, having a girth made of gold, Ṛg-veda IV. 2, 8.)
हेर: हेर हेर, अम्, n. (perhaps fr. rt. 1. हि, or connected with rt. 1. हृ), a sort of crown or tiara; turmeric; demoniacal illusion.
हेरिक: हेरिक, अस्, m. [cf. हैरिक], a spy, secret emis-sary or agent, (said to be also written हेरक।)
हेरम्ब: हेरम्ब हेरम्ब, अस्, m., N. of Gaṇeśa; a buffalo; a boastful hero (vain of his own valour); a particular Buddha (= हेरुक). —हेरम्ब-जननी, f. ‘mother of Gaṇeśa,’ Durgā. —हेरम्ब-मन्त्र, अस्, m. a particular Mantra (sacred to Gaṇeśa). —हेरम्ब-हट्ट, अस्, m., N. of a country, (said to be one of the provinces of the Deccan.)
हैरम्ब: हैरम्ब, अस्, ई, अम्, connected with or belong-ing to Gaṇeśa; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a sect.
हेरुक: हेरुक हेरुक, अस्, m. an attendant on Mahā-kāla or Śiva; (with Buddhists) an inferior Buddha.
हेल्: हेल् 1. हेल्। See rt. हेड्, p. 1176.
हेल् 2. हेल् or हेऌ (connected with rt. हिल्) = rt. हेड्, q. v.; cl. 1. A. हेलते, &c., to disregard, slight; to be angry, &c.
हेलञ्ची: हेलञ्ची, f. a kind of pot-herb (= हिल-मोचि).
हेलन: हेलन, अम्, n. the act of disregarding, slighting, disrespect, contempt [cf. अव-हेलन]; sporting amorously, wanton dalliance; [cf. rt. हिल्।]
हेला: हेला, f. disrespect, contempt [cf. अव-हेला]; wan-ton sport, amorous dalliance, manner or gesture of lovers, play, sport, pastime, pleasure, delight, (हेलया, inst. c. sportively, out of mere sport or pastime, for amusement); facility, ease, (हेलया, with the greatest ease, easily, at once); moonlight; pausing in a note or shaking as in music. —हेला-राज, अस्, m., N. of a commentator.
हेलि: 1. हेलि, इस्, f. dalliance, wanton sport, amorous embrace.
हेलि 2. हेलि, इस्, m. (probably borrowed fr. Gr. ἥλιος), the sun.
हेलित: हेलित, अस्, आ, अम्, disregarded, neglected, slighted.
हेलावुक्क: हेलावुक्क हेलावुक्क, अस्, m. (= हेडावुक्क), a horse-dealer, horse-seller.
हेलु: हेलु हेलु, N. of a village in Kaśmīra. —हेलु-ग्राम, अस्, m. the village Helu. —हेलु-दिण्ण, अस्, आ, अम् (दिण्ण Prākṛt for दत्त), pre-sented with (the village) Helu, having received Helu as a present.
हेष्: हेष् हेष् [cf. rt. ह्रेष्], cl. 1. A. हेषते, जिहेषे, हेषितुम्, to neigh (as a horse), whinny; to make any inarticulate sound, bray, roar; [cf. Gr. γίννος; Lat. hinnio (for hisnio), hin-nulus.]
हेष: हेष, अस्, m. neighing; a neigh, braying, roaring. —हेष-क्रतु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. making a neighing or roaring sound, roaring, (in Ṛg-veda III. 26, 5. said of lions; according to Sāy. हेष-क्रतवः = हेषा-रवस्य क्रतुः करणं येषां ते।)
हेषस्: हेषस्, Ved. (probably) neighing, braying; sound-ing, (in Ṛg-veda X. 89. 12. Sāy. explains हेषसा by शब्द-कारिण्या हेत्या।)
हेषा: हेषा, f. neighing (of horses), whinnying, braying.
हेषाय: हेषाय, Nom. A. हेषायते, -यितुम्, to neigh, whinny.
हेषित: हेषित, अम्, n. a neigh or any similar inarticulate sound, neighing, whinnying.
हेषिन्: हेषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, neighing; (ई), m. a horse.
हेहे: हेहे हे-हे, ind. (हे, q. v., repeated), a vo-cative particle (used in addressing, calling, or vocife-rating).
है: है है, ind. a vocative particle (used in calling or vociferating).
हैतुक: हैतुक हैतुक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. हेतु), causal, causative; argumentative, rationalistic; (अस्), m. a reasoner, arguer, logical reasoner; a follower of the Mīmāṃsā doctrines; one who requires a reason for everything, a rationalist, sceptic, causalist, sophist, heretic.
हैतुक्य: हैतुक्य, अम्, n. causality, causativeness, (अ-है-तुक्य, अम्, n. absence of interested motives.)
हैम: हैम 1. हैम, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 1. हेमन्), wintry, brumal, cold, frigid, freezing; (अम्), n. hoar-frost, dew.

हैम 2. हैम, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 2. हेमन्), golden, made of gold; of a golden yellow colour; (अस्), m. epithet of Śiva; the plant Gentiana Che-rayta; (आ or ई), f. yellow jasmine; (अम्), n. the lexicon of Hema-candra. —हैम-कोष, अस्, m. Hema-candra's lexicon. —हैम-चित्र-समुत्सेध, अस्, आ, अम्, enchased with golden pictures. —हैम-मुद्रा or हैम-मुद्रिका, f. a golden coin. —है-ममुद्रिक, अस्, ई, अम्, having or possessing a golden coin. —हैम-वल्कल, अस्, आ, अम्, having bark garments set with gold, clothed in gold. —हैमा-नेकार्थ (°म-अन्°), N. of a lexicon. —हैमी-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, become golden, turned into gold.
हैमन: 1. हैमन, अस्, ई, अम्, winterly, cold; growing in winter, suitable to winter; (अस्), m. the month Mārgaśīrṣa (= November-December); a kind of rice which grows in winter, = षष्टिक; (अस्, अम्), m. n. winter, the cold season, wintry weather.
2. हैमन, अस्, ई, अम्, golden, made of gold.
हैमन्त: हैमन्त, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. हेमन्त), wintry, cold; growing in winter, &c.; suitable to winter; (अस्, अम्), m. n. the winter season.
हैमन्तिक: हैमन्तिक, अस्, ई, अम्, wintry, cold, growing in winter; (अम्), n. a kind of rice, (see हैमन above.)
हैमल: हैमल, अस्, अम्, m. n. (fr. हिमल), winter, the cold season.
हैमवत: हैमवत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. हिम-वत्), snowy, covered with snow; flowing from the snowy moun-tain; bred in or belonging to the Himālaya moun-tains; (अस्), m. a sort of poison; (ई), f. epithet of the goddess Pārvatī; the river Ganges (which rises in the Himālaya mountains); N. of a wife of Viśvā-mitra; a kind of drug or perfume (= रेणुका); a kind of white orris root; common flax (= अतसी); the plant Svarṇa-kṣīrī; a kind of myrobalan (= हरीतकी); the tawny grape, (in some of these last senses probably to be connected with 2. हैम below); (अम्), n. Bhārata-varṣa or India. —है-मवत-वर्ष, अम्, n. India.
हैयङ्गवीन: हैयङ्गवीन हैयङ्गवीन, अम्, n. (fr. ह्यस् + गो with insertion of nasal), clarified butter pre-pared from yesterday's milking; butter prepared only a day before it is used, fresh butter.
हैरण्यगर्भ: हैरण्यगर्भ हैरण्यगर्भ, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. हिरण्य-गर्भ), belonging to Hiraṇya-garbha; (अस्), m. the offspring of Hiraṇya-garbha (i. e. Manu Svāyambhuva, son of Brahmā).
हैरण्यवासस्: हैरण्यवासस् हैरंयवासस्, आस्, आस्, अस् (fr. हिरण्य + वासस्), having a golden dress or covering; (आस्), m. an arrow.
हैरण्यस्तूप: हैरण्यस्तूप हैरण्यस्तूप, अस्, ई, अम्, be-longing to Hiraṇya-stūpa, q. v.; (अस्), m. a patro-nymic, (see हिरण्य-स्तूप।)
हैरिक: हैरिक हैरिक, अस्, m. (probably connected with rt. 1. हृ, cf. हरिक), a thief.
हैहय: हैहय हैहय, अस्, m. (thought by some to be connected with हय, a horse), N. of a tribe of people (said to have been descendants of Yadu; they are described in the Purāṇas as separated into five divisions, viz. the Tāla-jaṅghas, Vīti-hotras, Āvantyas, Tuṇḍikeras, and Jātas; they are said to have overrun parts of India along with the Śakas or Scythian tribes); N. of the great grandson of Yadu; of Arjuna Kārtavīrya (as ninth in descent from Haihaya or as king of the Haihayas; he is said to have had a thousand arms; see कार्तवीर्य).
हैहेय: हैहेय, अस्, m. Arjuna Kārtavīrya (= हैहय).
हो: हो हो, ind. a vocative particle used in calling to a person or in challenging (ho! hallo!); also expressive of surprise.
होड्: होड् होड् [cf. rts. हुड्, हूड्], cl. 1. A. होडते, जुहोडे, &c., to disregard, disrespect (= rt. हेड्); cl. 1. P. होडति, जुहोड, &c., to go.
होड: होड, अस्, m. a raft, float, boat (= तरान्धु); a title of a particular class of Kāyasthas; a title of Śrotriya Brāhmans in Bengal.
होडा: होडा होडा, f. (according to the Laghu-kaumudī), a young girl (in the language of the Vedas).
होडृ: होडृ होडृ, आ, m. (said to be fr. rt. हुड्; cf. हुर् under rt. हुर्छ्), a robber, foot-pad, high-way-robber.
होढ: होढ 1. होढ, अस्, आ, अम् [cf. हुर् under rt. हुर्छ्], stolen; (अम्), n. stolen goods; [cf. 2. स-होढ, p. 1102.]
2. होढ, Nom. A. होढते, होढायते, see Vopa-deva XXI. 7.
होतृ: होतृ होतृ, ता, त्री, तृ (according to Uṇādi-s. II. 96. fr. rt. हु; according to others in the sense ‘priest,’ fr. rt. ह्वे), sacrificing, offering oblations with fire, a sacrificer; (ता), m. an offerer of an oblation or burnt-offering (with fire); a priest who at a sacrifice invokes the gods or recites the prayers of the Ṛg-veda, a priest conversant with the Ṛg-veda, (one of the four kinds of officiating priest, see ऋत्व्-इज्, p. 181; properly the Hotṛ priest has three assistants, sometimes called Puruṣas, viz. the Maitrā-varuṇa, Acchāvāka, and Grāva-stut; to these are sometimes added three others, making seven Hotṛ priests in all, viz. the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, Agnīdhra or Agnīdh, and Potṛ, though these last are properly assigned to the Brahman priest; sometimes the Neṣṭṛ is substituted for the Grāva-stut); a sacri-ficing priest (in general); an epithet of Agni or fire, (in this sense fr. rt. हु); (त्री), f. one of the eight Mūrtis or Tanus, i. e. material manifestations of Śiva, (but this may be referred to होत्रिन्, see शिव।) —होता-पोतारौ, m. du. (nom. c.) the Hotṛ and Potṛ priests. —होतृ-वूर्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (a rite) in which a priest has to be chosen. —होतृ-षदन, अम्, n. the Hotṛ's seat or place where the Hotṛ sits at a sacrifice, (said to be near the उत्तर-वेदि।) —होतृ-संस्था-जप, N. of a liturgical treatise. —होतॄकार (°तृ-ॠक्° or -ऌक्°), अस्, m. the mother of the Hotṛ (according to Vopa-deva, the letters ॠ, ऌ, and ॡ being employed as mystical formularies by the Hotṛ, see ॡ).
होतृक: होतृक, अस्, m. a minor Hotṛ priest or assistant of the Hotṛ, (see above.)
होत्र: होत्र, अम्, n. (fr. rt. हु), anything intended or fit for offering with fire (generally clarified butter); the clarified butter so offered (= हविस्); a burnt-offering, oblation with fire, a sacrifice, (in Ṛg-veda II. 36, 1. होत्र = होतुर् याग।) —होत्र-वाहन, अस्, m. ‘bearer of the burnt-offering,’ a proper N. —होत्राशंसिन् (°र-आश्°), ई, m. ‘a repeater of the Hotṛ verses,’ a particular minor Hotṛ priest, (the Potṛ, the Neṣṭṛ, and the Āgnīdhra belong to this class.)
होत्रक: होत्रक, अस्, m., Ved. an inferior Hotṛ priest, (the Maitrāvaruṇa or Pra-śāstṛ, the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, and the Acchāvāka belong to this class; see हो-तृक।)
होत्रा: होत्रा, f. an oblation, sacrifice; praise (= स्तुति); speech (= वाच्, Naigh. I. 11); N. of a Vedic god-dess (said to have been the wife of Agni).
होत्रिन्: होत्रिन्, ई, m. a sacrificing priest; the priest who offers the oblation.
होत्री: होत्री, f. See under होतृ above.
होत्रीय: होत्रीय, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to an oblation, connected with a burnt-offering, &c.; (अस्), m. the priest who offers an oblation; (अम्), n. any place or chamber where oblations are offered, a sacrificial chamber.
होम: होम, अस्, m. the act of making an oblation to the Devas or gods by casting clarified butter into the fire (accompanied with prayers and invocations; this is regarded as one of the five Mahā-yajñas and called Deva-yajña, see महा-यज्ञ, देव-यज्ञ); an oblation of clarified butter, oblation with fire, burnt-offering; a sacrifice, (अयुत-होम, अस्, m. a sacri-fice of 10,000 burnt-offerings to the planets.) —हो-म-कुण्ड, अम्, n. a hole in the ground for receiv-ing the consecrated fire for an oblation; [cf. अग्नि-कुण्ड, हवनी।] —होम-द्रव्य, अम्, n. anything employed for a Homa-sacrifice or oblation. —होम-द्रव्य-परिमाण, N. of a Pari-śiṣṭa of the Sāma-veda. —होम-धान, अम्, n. a sacrificial chamber. —होम-धान्य, अम्, n. sacrificial grain; sesamum (= तिल). —होम-धूम, अस्, m. the smoke of a burnt-offering or sacrificial fire. —होम-भस्मन्, अ, n. the ashes of a burnt-offering. —होम-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, one who has offered an oblation or performed sacrifice. —होम-वेला, f. the time for the burnt-offering. —होम-शाला, f. a chamber or place for keeping the sacred fire for oblations. —होम-स्व-रोत्तर (°र-उत्°), N. of a work. —होमाग्नि (°म-अग्°), इस्, m. sacrificial fire, the fire for an oblation.
होमक: होमक, अस्, m. the priest who offers the oblation (= होतृ).
होमन्: होमन्, अ, n. an oblation, &c. (= होम above).
होमि: होमि, इस्, m. clarified butter; fire; water.
होमिन्: होमिन्, ई, m. the priest who makes the oblation (of clarified butter &c.); an offerer of any oblation (e. g. तिल-होमिन्, an offerer of sesamum).
होमीय: होमीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating or belonging to an oblation, fit for an oblation, belonging to a sacrifice. —होमीय-द्रव्य, अम्, n. anything used for an oblation (as clarified butter).
होम्य: होम्य, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to or fit for an oblation; (अम्), n. clarified butter.
हौतृक: हौतृक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. होतृ), relating or belonging to the Hotṛ priest, sacerdotal.
हौतृक हौतृक, हौत्न, हौत्र। See p. 1178, col. 3.
हौत्न: हौत्न, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. IV. 105. fr. rt. हु), the offerer of an oblation.
हौत्र: हौत्र, अम्, n. (fr. होत्र), the office or function of a Hotṛ priest. —हौत्र-प्रयोग, N. of a prac-tical hand-book for the Hotṛ priests. —हौत्र-सूत्र, अम्, n., N. of certain Sūtras by Kātyāyana.
हौत्रक: हौत्रक, अम्, n., N. of a Pari-śiṣṭa of the Yajur-veda.
हौम्य: हौम्य, अस्, आ or -मी, अम् (fr. होम), belonging to or fit for a Homa or oblation; (अम्), n. clarified butter. —हौम्य-धान्य, अम्, n. sacrificial grain, sesamum.
होरा: होरा होरा, f. (borrowed fr. Gr. ὥρα), the rising of a zodiacal sign; part of the duration of a sign; an hour; a mark, line; a particular scientific work or science, (probably astrological.) —होरा-फल, अम्, n. the result or effect of the rising of a sign. —होरा-मकरन्द, N. of an astrological work. —होरा-शास्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a work by Satya. —होरा-सार-सुधानिधि, N. of a work by Nārāyaṇa.
होरिलसिंह: होरिलसिंह होरिल-सिंह, अस्, m. a proper N.
होलक: होलक होलक, अस्, m. chick-pea or pulse half parched in the pod or fried on a grass fire.
होलसिंह: होलसिंह होल-सिंह, अस्, m. a proper N.
होलाक: होलाक होलाक, अस्, m. a kind of sweating (practised for the cure of certain diseases).
होलाका: होलाका होलाका, f. (perhaps fr. the sound made in singing), the spring festival held at the ap-proach of the vernal equinox (commonly called Hūlī or Holī, and one of the most popular festivals in India; it is said to be dedicated to Kṛṣṇa and the Gopīs, and is properly celebrated during the ten days pre-ceding the full moon of the month Phālguna, q. v., but usually only for the last three or four days ending with the full moon; the chief observances described are sprinkling one another with red or yellow powder in sport, addressing passers-by with jokes, singing songs in praise of the young Kṛṣṇa, and lighting fires around which rude frolics are practised; in Marāṭhī the name Holī is said to be applied also to the pile prepared for the fire; in some parts of India the Holī festival corresponds to or immediately precedes the Dola-yātrā).
होली: होली (or according to some also होलिका, हूली), the common designation of the Holākā festival or of the song sung during the festival.
होहौ: होहौ हो-हौ, ind. a vocative particle (ho! ho there! hallo!), an interjection used in calling or challenging.
हौ: हौ, ind. a vocative particle, = हो-हौ above.

ह्वे: ह्वे ह्वे (in some of its forms identical with rt. हु at p. 1174, and several derivatives seem to recognize another rt. हु or हू = ह्वे), cl. 1. P. A. ह्वयति, -ते, जुहाव (identical in form with Perf. of rt. हु), जुहुवे (in Ṛg-veda I. 48, 14. जुहूरे = जुह्विरे), ह्वास्यति, -ते, अह्वत्, अह्वत or अह्-वास्त, Prec. हूयात्, ह्वासीष्ट (Vedic forms Pres. 1st sing. हवे or हुवे, 3rd sing. हवते, 1st pl. हवामहे, ह्वामहे, हूमहे, होम, 3rd pl. ह-वन्ते; Impf. 3rd pl. हवन्त; Pot. 1st pl. हु-वेम; Perf. 3rd sing. हुवे, (आ)जुह्वे, 3rd pl. जुहुरे, जुहूरे; Aor. 1st sing. अह्वे, 3rd pl. अहू-षत), ह्वातुम् (Ved. Inf. हवीतवे, हुवध्यै), to call; to call to; to call upon, invoke; to chal-lenge; to name; to seek, ask, pray, beg; to emu-late, vie with: Pass. हूयते (identical in form with Pass. of rt. हु), Aor. अह्वायि, &c., to be called, &c.: Caus. ह्वाययति, -यितुम्, Aor. अजूहवत्: Desid. of Caus. जुहावयिषति: Desid. जुहूषति, -ते: Intens. जोहूयते, जोहवीति, जोहोति (Impf. अजोहवीत्, 3rd pl. अजोहवुः, Pres. part. जोहुवत्), to call on, invoke; [cf. according to some, Gr. βοή, βοάω, pro-bably ἀΰω, ἰωή; Lat. re-boare, perhaps voveo, vo-tum; Goth. vôpjan; Old Germ. hweion, hrôfu, ruafu; Mod. Germ. Rufe; Angl. Sax. hweop, wepan; Old Icel. hvîa, ‘to neigh;’ Slav. zv-a-ti, ‘to call;’ Hib. guilim, ‘I bewail.’]
हूति: हूति, इस्, f. calling; invocation; calling defiantly, challenging.
हूत्वा: हूत्वा, ind. having called, having challenged.
ह्वयत्: ह्वयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, calling out; challenging, vying with.
ह्वातृ: ह्वातृ, ता, त्री, तृ, who or what calls, a caller, challenger.
ह्वान: ह्वान, अम्, n. the act of calling; a cry, noise; [cf. कु-ह्वान।]
ह्वानीय: ह्वानीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be called or invoked.
ह्वायिन्: ह्वायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, calling, invoking, challenging.
ह्वेय: ह्वेय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be called; to be invoked.
